title: Findings (cross-skill handoff)
description: Shared JSON shape emitted by producer skills (review, standards, c4-reverse-engineer) and consumer skill reports (apply-review). The document-level 'source' field discriminates which finding subtype is used and which top-level fields are required.

schema_version.description: SemVer string, aligned with the plugin version at the time the document was written (.claude-plugin/plugin.json version). Consumers read this to identify which plugin release produced the envelope.

source.description: The producing skill, or the shape of the output for consumer skills. `update-pr` is absent deliberately — it emits review-shaped findings (with optional `pr_comment` fields) under `source: "review"`.

scoring.description: Scoring mode used by the producing review run. Absent means categorical (the five-dimension rubric). simple means findings carry direct severity + confidence and omit the categorical dimensions. Only meaningful for source: review.

run_id.description: Identifier of the orchestrator run that produced this envelope, matching costs.json `run_id` and the `review.run_id` OTEL resource attribute on every sub-agent. Present only for orchestrated runs (source: review); the local run ledger under .tmp-review/ is wiped by the next run, so this is the durable link from findings back to the agents that produced them.

orchestrating_session_id.description: Claude Code session that launched the run. Its own spend is NOT in costs.json — the orchestrator issues no model calls and the session outlives the run — so this is a join key, not a cost. Matches the `review.orchestrating_session_id` OTEL resource attribute.

run_report.description: Per-step outcome of the orchestrated run that produced this envelope. Answers 'what ran and what did not' without reading logs or the run ledger (.tmp-review/costs.json, which the next run wipes). Complements issues[]: issues say what went wrong, steps say what ran at all — a stage that degraded quietly (a validator batch that never dispatched, a selector that fell back to the full roster) is a step row even when it produced no issue. The render step itself is absent by construction: this report is written before rendering.

harness.description: Agent CLI that ran the agents, e.g. claude or codex.

status.description: Worst step outcome: failed if any step failed, degraded if any step degraded, otherwise ok. A skipped step alone is not a degradation.

supplementary.description: Optional source-specific metadata that the render script uses to produce supplementary markdown. Not part of the cross-skill handoff contract; consumers may ignore it. Shape is defined by each producer skill.

runtime_scope.description: Where the affected code executes in the deployment lifecycle. Values listed from least to most severe: documentation — non-executable content (e.g., markdown, comments, READMEs). tooling — developer tooling and local scripts that never execute in CI or production. ci — CI/CD pipelines and build infrastructure; executes during integration but not at production runtime. Findings about missing or incomplete tests use ci because tests execute in CI, not in production. Use service-internal or service-external only for findings about defects in production runtime code, not for test coverage gaps. service-internal — production runtime code not directly exposed to untrusted input. service-external — production runtime code directly exposed to external users or untrusted input. This axis measures input exposure, not output visibility: code whose output reaches an external consumer (an exported audit record, an API response, a UI status) is still service-internal when untrusted input does not reach it. When a finding identifies both a production defect and a test gap, report them as separate findings: the defect uses service-internal or service-external; the test gap uses ci.

runtime_scope_justification.description: Cite the file/module and explain its role in the deployment lifecycle. For test coverage gaps, cite the test directory and the code under test.

failure_mode.description: The category of consequence if the issue manifests. The failure must be current — 'if a future regression occurs' is not a failure mode; use unclear when the system currently works correctly and the finding is about a coverage or observability gap. Values listed from least to most severe: unclear — no specific failure scenario can be identified; the issue is stylistic, structural, or speculative. confusion — misleads a human reading an artifact: documentation, comments, identifiers, log text, error strings. It does not cover values the system writes: a wrong value in a persisted record, an API response, an exported event, or a status served to a UI is the system's output, not an artifact a human reads, and is degraded-behavior even when the wrong value is itself a label like 'success'. build-break — prevents successful build, lint, or test execution; blocks CI but does not affect running systems. degraded-behavior — the system produces incorrect results, loses functionality, or behaves unexpectedly under specific conditions, but remains available. crash-or-outage — the system becomes unavailable (e.g., process crash, unhandled exception, resource exhaustion, denial of service). data-loss-or-security — the system's data integrity, confidentiality, or security posture is compromised (e.g., data corruption, exfiltration, unauthorized access, privilege escalation, injection, information disclosure).

failure_mode_justification.description: Describe the specific failure scenario — what goes wrong, for whom, and under what conditions. For unclear, explain why no specific failure scenario can be identified.

evidence_quality.description: How strongly the finding is grounded in observable code evidence. 'demonstrated' requires demonstrating a failure in the code, not demonstrating the absence of a test. Proving that a test does not exist is not demonstrated evidence of a defect — use inferred if you can identify a plausible failure scenario the test would catch, or speculative if you cannot. Values listed from least to most severe: speculative — suspected based on patterns or general best practices; no concrete code path identified. inferred — a plausible scenario is visible in the code structure, but the conclusion requires assumptions about runtime state, configuration, or input that are not verified. demonstrated — a specific code path is traced from input to problematic outcome, citing concrete lines; the issue is visible from the code alone without runtime assumptions.

evidence_quality_justification.description: Summarize the evidence chain — what was traced, what was verified, and what (if anything) remains assumed.

trace_origin.description: How far back the agent traced to establish reachability. The trace must lead to a problematic outcome — tracing to working code and noting 'but there is no test' is not an entry-point trace. For test coverage gaps, use local because the finding observes a single code site (the missing test) without tracing a failure through callers. Values listed from least to most severe: local — observed at a single code site without tracing callers or callees. component — traced within a module or package boundary (e.g., function A calls function B which exhibits the issue); external reachability is not established. entry-point — traced from an identified external entry point (e.g., API handler, CLI command, CI trigger, user action) through the call chain to the problematic code.

trace_origin_justification.description: For entry-point: name the entry point and trace the path to the problematic outcome. For component: identify the module boundary. For local: explain why no caller trace was performed.

effort_to_fix.description: Estimated remediation cost. Not used in criticality assessment; used for prioritization. Values: trivial — a one-line change, rename, or config tweak with no design decisions. small — a localized fix within one file or function. moderate — changes spanning multiple files or functions, potentially requiring test updates. large — requires architectural changes, new abstractions, or significant refactoring.

effort_to_fix_justification.description: Describe the fix approach and why it requires the stated level of effort.

confidence.description: Reviewer confidence from the simple scoring mode. low-confidence findings carry severity needs-review.

finding_id.description: Finding ID from the consumed Findings-*.json, e.g. C0, I3, S1.

outcome.description: applied = committed; skipped = no changes made; failed = attempted but errored; pending-commit = implemented in the working tree but left uncommitted (batch mode).

detail.description: Short free-text note (e.g. reason for skip/fail, or a human-readable summary).

commit_sha.description: Commit SHA of the change produced by this finding. Required semantics: set when outcome is 'applied'; absent for skipped/failed/pending-commit.

error_kind.description: Machine-readable error classification. Populated only when outcome is 'failed'; mirrors issue.kind so auditors can aggregate failures by cause.

run_step.description: One pipeline step and how it ended.

step.description: Pipeline step name, e.g. scope, select, review, validate.

status.description: ok = ran and nothing was lost. degraded = ran, but part of its work did not land (some agents failed, a fallback was taken). skipped = deliberately not run for this scope or mode. failed = aborted the run.

detail.description: Human-readable outcome: counts, which agents failed, why it was skipped.
